title: Finite cohomology of a sufficiently large specified Chow twist
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], where $T$ is affine with Noetherian ring $R=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Let $i:W\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $\pi:Y\to W$ a proper morphism, $N$ a finite coordinate type, and $j:Y\to\mathbf P(N;T)$ a closed immersion with $j\circ\mathrm{pr}=\pi\circ i\circ f$ in diagrammatic order [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Set $L=j^*\rho^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(N;\mathbf Z)}(1)$, where $\rho$ is the projection to the integral projective model and the twist is [def-pc-projective-space-twist], using module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. There exists $n\in\mathbf N$ such that $G_n=i_*\pi_*(L^{\otimes n})$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent] and, for every $q\geq0$, $H^q(X,G_n)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is a finite $R$-module, with scalars restricted along $f.\mathrm{appTop}$. Neither integrality of $W$ nor birationality of $\pi$ is assumed.

proof.text: The graph (j, pi) is a closed immersion into projective space over W. Its twist agrees with L, making L relatively ample for pi and pi followed by i followed by f. Reindex finite nonempty coordinates by ULift (Fin (m+1)); empty coordinates give empty Y and zero modules.

The affine Noetherian T and the proper source and intermediate schemes are Noetherian. Apply relative Serre vanishing to the structure module to choose a common twist n with all positive higher images zero for both projective morphisms.

On affine opens of W, projective cohomology finiteness and quasi-coherent localization show that pi_* L^n is associated to a finite section module. The coherent/finite-type equivalence proves coherence independently of general proper coherence; closed pushforward preserves coherence.

Leray for pi, whose positive images vanish, and exact closed pushforward identify H^q(X,G_n) with H^q(Y,L^n). Naturality with multiplication by global sections gives Gamma(T,top)-linear comparisons. Projective finiteness on the affine base and transport along these comparisons prove finiteness.

theorem exists_chow_twist_finite_cohomology {X W T Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ T) [IsProper f] [IsAffine T] [IsNoetherianRing Γ(T, ⊤)]
    (i : W ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (π : Y ⟶ W) [IsProper π]
    (N : Type u) [Finite N] (j : Y ⟶ ℙ(N; T)) [IsClosedImmersion j]
    (hj : j ≫ (ℙ(N; T) ↘ T) = π ≫ i ≫ f) :
    let L := (pullback j).obj
      ((pullback (ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt N T)).obj
        (Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule N (ULift.{u} ℤ)) 1))
    ∃ n : ℕ,
      RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace
        ((pushforward i).obj ((pushforward π).obj (L.tensorPow n))) ∧
      (∀ q : ℕ,
        letI : Module Γ(T, ⊤)
          (((pushforward i).obj ((pushforward π).obj (L.tensorPow n))).H q) :=
            Module.compHom _ f.appTop.hom
        Module.Finite Γ(T, ⊤)
          (((pushforward i).obj ((pushforward π).obj (L.tensorPow n))).H q))
